text:
mira: quick idea 64 small in-band "progframe" for streaming responses so gateway can resume without blind replay of whole request. checksum + monotonic seq.

sam: how is this different from current resume tokens?
mira: current tokens are opaque and backend-specific. progframes are emitted in-stream and are client-visible hints the gateway can persist briefly. helps migration between workers and reduces duplicate output on retries.

raj: proto sketch? keep it tiny and backward-compatible.
mira: sketch: PROGFRAME v1: seq:u64 | bytes_emitted:u64 | tokens:u32 | hint:"boundary|periodic" | crc32:hex. emit every N tokens or on sentence boundary.

kevin: gateway semantics: optional. store last frame per-request in-memory with TTL (default 30s). gateway asks new backend to resume from seq+crc if worker dies.

sam: side-effects are still a problem. repeating external webhooks could happen. we need an idempotency hook.

raj: agree; combine with backend-advertised resume-capable flag and optional idempotency_key when side-effects occur. gateway only resumes when compatible.

kevin: perf: bound memory by storing a single fixed-size record per stream and an LRU eviction. metrics: progframe_emitted, resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_fallback.

mira: partial frames: CRC computed over canonicalized payload so truncated frames are ignored. gateway requires full frame receipt.

raj: gating: only resume when backend/version matches progframe version. fallback policy per-route: fail-open or full retry.

kevin: implementation tasks: wire proto + canonical CRC, gateway in-memory store + TTL, backend resume API, metrics + rollout flags.

mira: I'll draft RFC and schedule 30-min sync with runtime/serving. default ttl 30s, per-route override.

sam: +1

raj: +1
